brief.topic: Task success rate vs user satisfaction as the north-star metric for an AI assistant
brief.audience: PMs choosing metrics for AI assistants
constraints: Illustrative numbers labelled on screen and in caption

coreInsight: Users rate how an AI answer feels, not whether it got the job done, so satisfaction can rise while task success falls; lead with task success wherever the outcome can be checked.

hooks.notes: Four words that contain the whole tension.

hooks.text: Your thumbs-up rate is lying to you.
CSAT or task success: which is your AI’s north star?
hooks.notes: Clear but reads like a textbook prompt.

caption.opening: A confident, friendly wrong answer often gets a thumbs up.
body: That’s why satisfaction and task success can move in opposite directions. Users rate how an answer feels; they often can’t tell whether it was right.

How to choose:
→ lead with task success when the job has a checkable outcome (booked, resolved, correct)
→ lead with satisfaction when quality is a matter of taste (tone, style)
→ track both, and treat a gap between them as a bug report
(The 82% vs 54% in the reel is an illustrative example, not data from a real product.)

claims.text: User satisfaction ratings for AI answers can rise while task success falls, because users often cannot judge correctness; task success should lead where outcomes are checkable.
82% thumbs-up rate vs 54% of tasks actually completed.
